name: Question 10
problem:
Consider the function $y=({x}^{2}+3x)^{x}.$ Its derivative is given by 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=({x}^{2}+3x)^{x-1}\cdot g(x).
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=({x}^{2}+3x)^{x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{2}+3x)^{x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3x))+(x)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3x)+x\cdot (\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+3x}\cdot 2x+3) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3x)+\frac{2{x}^{2}+3x}{{x}^{2}+3x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =y(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3x)+\frac{2{x}^{2}+3x}{{x}^{2}+3x})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=({x}^{2}+3x)^{x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =({x}^{2}+3x)^{x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3x)+\frac{2{x}^{2}+3x}{{x}^{2}+3x}) \\  & =({x}^{2}+3x)^{x}(\frac{({x}^{2}+3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3x)}{{x}^{2}+3x}+\frac{2{x}^{2}+3x}{{x}^{2}+3x}) \\  & =({x}^{2}+3x)^{x-1}(({x}^{2}+3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3x)+(2{x}^{2}+3x)).\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $g(x)=({x}^{2}+3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3x)+(2{x}^{2}+3x).$

Question 10
?

Consider the function y=(x2+3x)x. Its derivative is given by

dydx=(x2+3x)x−1⋅g(x).

Find the function g(x).

a
(x2+x)ln⁡(x2+3x)+x2−3x
b
(3x2+x)ln⁡(x2+3x)+x2+3x
c
(x2+3x)ln⁡(x2+3x)+2x2+3x
d
(x2+x)ln⁡(x2+3x)+2x2+x
e
(x2−x)ln⁡(x2+3x)+3x2+2x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We have the function

y=(x2+3x)x.

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

ln⁡y=ln⁡((x2+3x)x)ln⁡y=xln⁡(x2+3x)

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to x:

ddx(ln⁡y)=ddx(xln⁡(x2+3x))1y⋅dydx=ddx(x)⋅(ln⁡(x2+3x))+(x)⋅ddx(ln⁡(x2+3x))1y⋅dydx=1⋅ln⁡(x2+3x)+x⋅(1x2+3x⋅2x+3)1y⋅dydx=ln⁡(x2+3x)+2x2+3xx2+3x

Now, we solve for dydx:

dydx=y(ln⁡(x2+3x)+2x2+3xx2+3x)

Finally, we substitute y=(x2+3x)x:

dydx=(x2+3x)x(ln⁡(x2+3x)+2x2+3xx2+3x)=(x2+3x)x((x2+3x)ln⁡(x2+3x)x2+3x+2x2+3xx2+3x)=(x2+3x)x−1((x2+3x)ln⁡(x2+3x)+(2x2+3x)).

Therefore, g(x)=(x2+3x)ln⁡(x2+3x)+(2x2+3x).
